knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to $\sin(x - 3)\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}-\left(10 x - 30\right)\sin(x - 3)=\cos(x - 3)$ that satisfies $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 3)=2 \pi^{2}$. Assume that $3<x<3 + \pi$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first rearrange and separate, then integrate and apply the initial condition.

$$
y'=\frac{\cos(x - 3)}{\sin(x - 3)}+10 x - 30.
$$

Use $v=\sin(x - 3)$, so $\mathrm{d}v=\cos(x - 3)\mathrm{d}x$. On the given interval, sine is positive. Thus

$$
\int\mathrm{d}y=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{v}+\int \left(10 x - 30\right)\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
y=\ln(\sin(x - 3))+5 \left(x - 3\right)^{2}+C.
$$

At $x=\frac{\pi}{2} + 3$, $\sin(x - 3)=1$ and hence

$$
2 \pi^{2}=\frac{5 \pi^{2}}{4}+C,\qquad C=\frac{3 \pi^{2}}{4}.
$$

Therefore $y=5 \left(x - 3\right)^{2} + \ln{\left(\sin{\left(x - 3 \right)} \right)} + \frac{3 \pi^{2}}{4}$.
